faq.q: What is the cheapest yacht for a hen party in Marbella in 2035?
faq.a: The most affordable option is the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax), both priced on request but typically under €500 for 2 hours. For a group of 9, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 at €749 for 2 hours offer the best value, including skipper, drinks, and snacks.

faq.q: Are drinks and food included in the hen party yacht charter price?
faq.a: Yes, every charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. For larger groups or special requests (e.g., champagne, cocktail bar, or a full catered menu), we can arrange upgrades – just ask via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Do we need to pay extra for a skipper or fuel?
faq.a: No. A licensed skipper and all fuel are included in the quoted price. You don't need to worry about hidden costs – just show up at Puerto Banús and enjoy.

faq.q: Can we bring our own decorations or music for the hen party?
faq.a: Absolutely. Most groups bring banners, balloons, and a Bluetooth speaker. If you want a DJ or a professional sound system, we can arrange that for an additional fee – message us for a quote.

faq.q: What happens if it rains on our hen party day in 2035?
faq.a: Marbella averages 300+ sunny days a year, but if bad weather is forecast, we can reschedule or cancel with full refund up to 48 hours before departure. The skipper will also make a safety call on the day.

faq.q: How far in advance should we book a hen party yacht in Marbella for 2035?
faq.a: For peak summer (June–August) 2035, book at least 4–6 weeks ahead. Spring and autumn are more flexible, but weekends still fill fast. Early booking also locks in current prices.

faq.q: Is there a toilet on board?
faq.a: All our yachts over 10m (including Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, and larger) have at least one cabin with a toilet. Smaller boats like the Dubhe or Mariah SX21 do not – ask when booking if this is essential.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for a hen party charter?
faq.a: We offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before departure. Within 48 hours, a 50% fee applies. No-shows are charged in full. We recommend travel insurance for peace of mind.

data.body_html:
Planning a hen party in Marbella for 2035? A yacht charter is the ultimate way to celebrate, but costs can spiral if you don't know what to expect. This breakdown covers everything from boat hire to hidden extras, so you can budget accurately and avoid surprises. Whether you're a group of 5 or 12, we've got transparent pricing for every tier.

How much does a hen party yacht charter cost in Marbella in 2035?

Prices start from €749 for 2 hours on a Tier A boat (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39), which sleeps up to 9–11 guests. For a full day (8 hours), the same boats cost €2,299. If you want a superyacht experience, the Mangusta 80 (24m) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% Spanish VAT – no hidden fees.

Which boat is best for a hen party of 8–12 guests?

For groups of 8–12, the sweet spot is the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax). Both offer spacious sundecks, a cabin for changing, and plenty of shade. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is the party favourite thanks to its massive sunpad and included jet ski. All depart from Puerto Banús – Marbella's glitzy superyacht marina.

What's included in the price – and what's extra?

  • Included: Licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% VAT.
  • Extra cost: Premium catering (€25–€50/person), DJ (€300–€600), photographer (€200–€400), extra hours (pro rata), and jet ski rental on boats that don't include it.

For a full list of optional extras, contact us via WhatsApp – we'll tailor the package to your group.

Sample budget for a 4-hour hen party (10 guests, Tier A boat)

ItemCost (€)
Astondoa 40 – 4 hours€1,499
Premium catering (10 x €35)€350
DJ for 4 hours€400
Photographer (2 hours)€300
Total€2,549

That's €255 per person – competitive with a night out in Puerto Banús, but with far more memories.

When to book for the best price in 2035

Peak season (June–August) commands premium rates, but booking early locks in current prices. For a Saturday in July 2035, expect to pay 15–20% more than a weekday. Shoulder months (May, September, October) offer better value and still deliver 25°C+ temperatures. We recommend booking 4–6 weeks ahead for weekends, 2 weeks for weekdays.

Hidden costs to watch out for

Some operators add fuel surcharges, port fees, or cleaning fees. With us, everything except optional extras is included. The only potential extra is if you exceed the agreed time – overtime is charged at the pro-rata hourly rate. Always confirm the itinerary in advance to avoid clock-watching.

How to split the cost among the group

Most bridesmaids use Splitwise or a shared Revolut pot. For a 10-person group on a Tier A boat (4 hours), the base cost is €150/person. Add catering and DJ, and you're at ~€255/person. We recommend collecting a deposit (50%) upfront to secure the booking, then the balance 7 days before departure.
